clue.text: Printing process behind the scenes ?

definitions.meaning: lithographic printing where ink passes from plate to a rubber roller and then to paper
read as two words, away from the film or stage set, out of view of the cameras

explanation.surface: A printing method that happens out of public view.
explanation.definitionFit: Lithography via a blanket cylinder is the common commercial press method; 'off set' also means away from the filming area.

clue.text: It is worn if going up to central Manchuria

indicators.note: in a down clue going up means the word if is read from bottom to top
central picks the middle letters of the word Manchuria

explanation.surface: Something worn when travelling north to the heart of Manchuria.
explanation.walkthrough: 'going up' turns IF into FI; the central three letters of Manchuria give CHU.
explanation.definitionFit: A small triangular shawl draped over a woman's shoulders is an item of clothing.

clue.text: They customarily evade their duties

parts.note: customarily is read as concerning customs, and the duties are import taxes that contraband runners avoid paying

explanation.surface: People who habitually shirk their obligations.
explanation.walkthrough: 'customarily' seems to mean habitually, but points to Customs; 'duties' are taxes, not obligations.
explanation.definitionFit: Contraband runners bring goods past Customs without paying import tax.

clue.text: Translator with one French article, or three in one ?

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral one
une is the French feminine indefinite article

explanation.surface: An interpreter with a single French item, or a trio in one.
explanation.definitionFit: The adjective describes a Trinity, one being in three persons.

clue.text: Work quietly on net torn by adversary

parts.note: op is short for opus, a musical work
p (piano) is the musical marking for quietly

indicators.note: torn suggests the letters of the word net are ripped apart and rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone works silently on a fishing net that a rival has ripped.
explanation.walkthrough: 'torn' rearranges NET into ENT, which follows OP, P and ON.
explanation.definitionFit: Both words name a person on the other side in a contest or dispute.

clue.text: Muses, in a drunken state ?

parts.note: there are nine Muses, the ninth being one beyond eight, and the phrase is British slang for having drunk a little too much

explanation.surface: Someone ponders while intoxicated.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Muses' looks like a verb, ponders, but means the nine goddesses: nine is one more than eight.
explanation.definitionFit: A British idiom for slightly tipsy, literally one more drink than eight; the Muses number nine.

clue.text: A capital fellow is preserved in one kind of marble

indicators.note: preserved in means the word is is kept inside the name of the marble

parts.note: Parian marble is the fine white marble quarried on the Greek island of Paros

explanation.surface: A man from the capital ends up encased in marble.
explanation.definitionFit: A man from Paris, the French capital, is a native of that city.

clue.text: It is commonly doubled to describe HP

definitions.text: It is commonly doubled to describe HP

parts.words: It is commonly doubled to describe HP
parts.note: HP is hire purchase, buying on instalments, which British slang calls the ...-... because you seem ... to finish paying

explanation.surface: A word often repeated to describe a brand of sauce.
explanation.walkthrough: HP looks like the sauce or horsepower, but is hire purchase, the British instalment-buying scheme.
explanation.definitionFit: Repeated, the word gives British slang for buying on credit by instalments.

clue.text: On 'reflection, his self devotion transformed' him

definitions.text: On 'reflection, his self devotion transformed' him

parts.words: On 'reflection, his self devotion transformed' him
parts.note: the youth of Greek myth fell in love with his own reflection in a pool and was turned into a flower

explanation.surface: Thinking it over, his self-love changed him.
explanation.walkthrough: 'reflection' looks like thought but is his image in the water.
explanation.definitionFit: The mythical youth pined for his own image and became the flower that bears his name.

clue.text: He looks out for cases of double-crossing

definitions.text: He looks out for cases of double-crossing

parts.words: He looks out for cases of double-crossing
parts.note: an election official checking ballot papers watches for papers marked with two crosses, which are spoiled votes, not traitors

explanation.surface: A detective on the watch for betrayals.
explanation.walkthrough: 'double-crossing' suggests treachery, but here it means a voter putting two crosses on a ballot.
explanation.definitionFit: An election official examines ballot papers and rejects any marked more than once.

clue.text: Alter state railway

parts.note: VA is the abbreviation for Virginia, a US state

explanation.surface: Change the state-run rail network.
explanation.definitionFit: Both verbs mean to change or modify something.

clue.text: Russian writer whose gentlefolk nested

parts.note: points to the 1859 novel 'A Nest of Gentlefolk' (also 'Home of the Gentry') by the Russian author of 'Fathers and Sons'

explanation.surface: A Russian author whose upper-class characters settled down.
explanation.definitionFit: The Russian novelist wrote 'A Nest of Gentlefolk', so his gentlefolk are the ones in a nest.

clue.text: " That — again ! it had a dying fall " (T. Night)

definitions.text: That — again ! it had a dying fall

parts.words: That — again ! it had a dying fall
parts.note: the missing word completes Orsino's opening speech in Shakespeare's Twelfth Night, a musical phrase or melody

explanation.surface: A quotation from Twelfth Night with one word blanked out.
explanation.walkthrough: Orsino says 'That strain again! it had a dying fall', strain meaning a passage of music.
explanation.definitionFit: A musical phrase or tune fills the gap in Orsino's line about music being the food of love.

clue.text: Pain of a revolutionary from Argentina

parts.note: Che Guevara was the Argentine-born revolutionary of the Cuban revolution

explanation.surface: The suffering of an Argentine rebel.
explanation.definitionFit: Both nouns mean a dull continuous hurt.

clue.text: Innumerable noblemen, including the French

indicators.note: including means the word for noblemen holds the French article inside it

parts.note: counts are European noblemen
les is the French plural definite article

explanation.surface: Countless aristocrats, the French among them.
explanation.walkthrough: 'including' puts LES inside COUNTS, before its final S.
explanation.definitionFit: Too many to be numbered.

clue.text: To make a new arrangement is fair after study

indicators.note: after places the word for study ahead of the word for fair

parts.note: to read a subject at university is to study it
just means fair or equitable

explanation.surface: Rearranging things is fine once you have studied them.
explanation.definitionFit: To set something right again or adapt it to changed conditions is to re-adjust.

clue.text: Chucks out boys under the pier, say

indicators.note: say signals that the words are spoken, sounding like another word

parts.note: sons (boys) placed below jetty (pier) in a down clue

explanation.surface: Children playing beneath the seaside pier.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down entry, SONS under JETTY gives JETTYSONS, which 'say' makes sound like the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: To throw goods overboard, or discard anything unwanted.

clue.text: Confounded devils, so to break up the assembly!

indicators.note: confounded means mixed up, so the letters of devils and so are jumbled

explanation.surface: A curse on these devils for breaking up the meeting.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Confounded' looks like an oath but rearranges DEVILS and SO.
explanation.definitionFit: To end a parliament or meeting formally is to dissolve it.

clue.text: He 'makes barrels and thin mugs

indicators.note: makes is read as forming the letters of thin and mugs into something new

explanation.surface: A craftsman who produces casks and slender drinking mugs.
explanation.walkthrough: 'barrels' are gun barrels, not casks; THIN MUGS is rearranged.
explanation.definitionFit: A firearm maker builds guns, whose tubes are their barrels.

clue.text: A wee drap for Russian newsmen

definitions.meaning: in Scots a ... is a small cup or a small dram of drink
the Soviet official news agency, whose name abbreviated its Russian title

explanation.surface: A small Scotch for the visiting Russian journalists.
explanation.definitionFit: Scots uses the word for a small cup or tot, and the same letters named the Soviet news agency.

clue.text: Roof covering of yonder church'?

parts.note: yonder means that one over there

explanation.surface: Asking about the roof of the church over there.
explanation.definitionFit: Straw or reeds laid over a roof form a traditional covering.

clue.text: Emphasize the pressure associated with 12

definitions.meaning: to put weight on a word or point
12 across is strain, and strain and ... are paired terms of pressure on a material or person

explanation.surface: Underline how strain brings tension.
explanation.definitionFit: To lay weight on a point; physically, the force per area that produces strain.

clue.text: Down withthe bird.!

parts.note: the soft breast feathers of a sea duck give the word paired with down for quilts

explanation.surface: A protester's cry against a bird.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Down with' looks like a protest slogan; the feathers that go with this duck's name are down.
explanation.definitionFit: A northern sea duck whose breast feathers stuff quilts.

clue.text: Morally correct about a point concerning the 'race

indicators.note: about means the word for morally correct goes around the compass point

parts.note: ethical means morally right
N, north, is a point of the compass

explanation.surface: Being morally right about a point to do with race.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' puts N inside ETHICAL. 'point' is a compass point, not a dot.
explanation.definitionFit: An adjective relating to a people or ethnic group, an older form of ethnic.

clue.text: Man, perhaps, following a passage

indicators.note: following places the island after the letter given by a

parts.note: the Isle of Man is an island in the Irish Sea

explanation.surface: A man, perhaps, walking after someone down a corridor.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Man' is the Isle of Man, an island between Britain and Ireland.
explanation.definitionFit: A walkway between rows of seats, as in a church or theatre.

clue.text: Provide for a loud finish

parts.note: L is a recognised crossword abbreviation for loud, as on old volume switches
the end is the finish

explanation.surface: Arranging a grand finale for a show.
explanation.definitionFit: To lend something like dignity or support is to provide or contribute it.

clue.text: Darling, it was his' responsibility !

parts.note: Grace Darling's father William kept the Longstone light on the Farne Islands, from which she rowed out to a wreck in 1838

explanation.surface: Telling a loved one that something was his fault.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Darling' looks like an endearment but is Grace Darling, the English heroine who helped her keeper father rescue shipwreck survivors.
explanation.definitionFit: William Darling was keeper of the Longstone tower warning ships off the Farne rocks.

clue.text: Hungry to see: Turin in ruins?

indicators.note: in ruins says the letters of see and Turin are wrecked and put back in a new order

explanation.surface: Eager to visit an Italian city that has been devastated.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in ruins' rearranges SEE and TURIN together.
explanation.definitionFit: A literary word for greedy or ravenous.

clue.text: He lost a customer in Ben Battle

definitions.text: He lost a customer in Ben Battle

parts.words: He lost a customer in Ben Battle
parts.note: Ben Battle in Thomas Hood's poem 'Faithless Nelly Gray' had both legs shot off, so a stocking seller would sell him nothing

explanation.surface: A trader lost a client in a big battle.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Ben Battle' looks like a battle, but is the legless soldier of Hood's comic poem.
explanation.definitionFit: A dealer in stockings and socks needs customers with legs.
